fixes.explanation: Gilgal sounds like a fair guess, friend, but it's not the spot here. The text says the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there (Joshua 18:1). Shiloh is the answer on this one.

Careful, friend, it's the other way around. Joshua doesn't ask why they're in a hurry. He asks, "How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?" (Joshua 18:3). That's a question about putting things off, not rushing.

False is right, friend. Joshua never asks about a hurry. Seven tribes had not yet received their inheritance (Joshua 18:2), and he asks, "How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?" (Joshua 18:3). That's a how-long question, and I know a few of those myself.
Three men from each tribe, just like Joshua says (Joshua 18:4). Three, friend. I bet that's a lot of sandals wearing out by the end of the survey.

That's the job. Joshua says he will send them out "…survey the land and map it out, according to the inheritance of each." (Joshua 18:4). Then they return to him and divide the land into seven portions (Joshua 18:4-5). Looking, walking and writing it all down.

Altars are holy business, friend, but nobody hands out altar duty in this plan. Joshua sends the men out to "…survey the land and map it out…" (Joshua 18:4). Their whole assignment is the map. Mapmakers map, and that's the job on the list.

Lots, friend. Joshua says, "…I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God." (Joshua 18:6). The portions get mapped out and brought to him first. Then he casts the lots right there in the LORD's presence.

Caleb does get his own land in this book, so I see why he came to mind. Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as an inheritance (Joshua 14:13). But he's not the one here. When they finished distributing the land, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them (Joshua 19:49).

Last pick sounds like a sad ending for a man who did all this work, friend. But the text never calls it the last city. It says they gave him Timnath-serah "…as he requested." (Joshua 19:50). He asked for it.

Rebuilds, friend. Joshua "…rebuilt the city and settled in it." (Joshua 19:50). Both things are right there in one verse. He wasn't just handing out land for everybody else, because he put his hands to his own city too.
Emptying isn't in the verse, friend. The text says Joshua "…rebuilt the city and settled in it." (Joshua 19:50). Rebuilding is building up, not clearing out.
